evals.name: explicit-dotnet-prereq-check
evals.prompt: Check prerequisites for .NET. I'm about to scaffold an invoice-approval workflow with Dapr in C# and want to make sure my machine has everything first.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the OS, then checks the C# LSP plugin, .NET SDK, Docker/Podman and Dapr CLI in parallel, and reports pass/fail per prerequisite with install links for failures. If everything passes it points the user to create-workflow-dotnet. No project files are created.
expectations: Runs `uname -s` (OS detection) before the tool-version checks
Runs `dotnet --version` and judges the .NET check on the major version being 10 or higher (e.g. `10.0.100` and `11.0.100` pass, `9.0.100` fails)
Runs `docker info`, and runs `podman info` only if Docker is unavailable
Runs `dapr --version`, parses the `CLI version` line and accepts 1.18 or newer (e.g. `1.19.0` passes); it does not require the literal string `1.18`
Checks for the `csharp-lsp@claude-plugins-official` plugin by inspecting Claude settings, and does not run any `claude plugin` command
The `dotnet --version`, `docker info` and `dapr --version` calls are issued together in one parallel batch (same assistant turn), not one per turn
Final report lists C# LSP plugin, .NET SDK, Docker/Podman and Dapr CLI each with a pass or fail status; if all pass it says the user can proceed with the `create-workflow-dotnet` skill
Does not create any files or run `dotnet new`, and does not start the `create-workflow-dotnet` skill

evals.name: casual-is-my-machine-ready
evals.prompt: is my machine ready to build a dapr workflow in c#?
evals.expected_output: Casual phrasing still triggers the .NET prerequisite check. The same checks run (OS, C# LSP, .NET 10 SDK, Docker/Podman, Dapr CLI) and a per-check pass/fail report is shown. Python, uv and Aspire are not checked.
expectations: Runs `dotnet --version`, `dapr --version` and `docker info` (or `podman info`) rather than answering from general knowledge
States that the .NET SDK must be version 10 (.NET 10 SDK), linking https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download if the check fails
Report has one line or row per prerequisite (C# LSP plugin, .NET SDK, Docker/Podman, Dapr CLI) marked passed or failed
Does not run `python --version`, `uv --version` or `aspire --version` (those belong to other prerequisite skills)
Does not create a project, solution, or any file in the working directory
If every check passes, the final message mentions the `create-workflow-dotnet` skill as the next step

evals.name: windows-docker-not-installed
evals.prompt: I'm on Windows 11 and I haven't installed Docker yet. Can you still verify the rest of my .NET setup for Dapr Workflow and tell me what I need to fix?
evals.expected_output: The skill runs every check even though the user says Docker is missing. On Windows it retries failed commands via `powershell -Command`. It tries Podman before reporting the container runtime as failed, gives the Docker and Podman install links, and still reports .NET, Dapr CLI and C# LSP results. It does not try to install anything.
expectations: Treats the OS as Windows when `uname -s` returns a value starting with `MINGW`, `MSYS` or `CYGWIN` (Git Bash / MSYS2 / Cygwin) or when `uname` is not available
Runs `docker info` and, when it fails, also tries `podman info` before reporting the container-runtime check as failed
If a direct bash command fails, retries it as `powershell -Command "<cmd>"` (e.g. `powershell -Command "docker info"`) before declaring it missing
Still runs and reports the `dotnet --version`, `dapr --version` and C# LSP plugin checks; the Docker problem does not stop the run
If no container runtime is found, the report marks Docker/Podman as failed and includes https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/ and https://podman.io/docs/installation
Does not run any install command (e.g. `winget`, `choco`, `brew`, an installer download) and does not modify system settings
Does not tell the user they can proceed with `create-workflow-dotnet` while the Docker/Podman check is failing
